profile.reading:
Csquare IAD2-A sits at 22810 International Drive, Sterling, Virginia 20166, part of Csquare's IAD2 campus in Loudoun County, described by Csquare's own materials as "two additional pods" connected by dark fiber to the nearby IAD1 campus. Csquare (formerly branded Centersquare, launched April 2024 by Brookfield Infrastructure to combine Cyxtera, acquired out of Chapter 11 bankruptcy for $775 million in a deal completed January 2024, and Evoque, AT&T's divested data center business under Brookfield since 2019) went public via IPO on NASDAQ in July 2026 at $21.00 per share. Csquare's SEC Form S-1 property table lists this building individually as "IAD2_A," 49,427 square feet sellable, 55.7 percent leased and Csquare-owned as of March 31, 2026; Csquare's public spec sheet gives a campus-wide total of 48,169 square feet raised floor, 35.8 megawatts of utility power, 8.5 megawatts of UPS capacity, and 20 megawatts of generator capacity, with SOC 1/2 Type II, PCI-DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, and ISO 27001 certifications, notably without the ENERGY STAR rating Csquare cites for its IAD1 campus. Csquare does not name a power utility or year-opened date; Dominion Energy serves Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Csquare's Sterling, Virginia IAD2 campus sits within Loudoun County's Data Center Alley, the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world. Csquare's SEC S-1 discloses 389 megawatts of total sellable power capacity across its full 64-facility, 21-market portfolio as of March 31, 2026. The dark-fiber link Csquare describes between IAD2 and the nearby IAD1 campus allows customers at either site to interconnect directly without routing traffic through a third-party carrier hotel, a common colocation-industry practice for operators with multiple nearby buildings in the same metro.

sources.title: Csquare, Inc. Form S-1 Registration Statement

profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 95 (Centersquare): operator market page gives one combined Sterling IAD2 figure for what this registry splits into two clustered rows, combined figure recorded as context only and not applied per row, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete, no address applied.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to Centersquare. This session found that centersquaredc.com, the legacy domain matching this registry entire Centersquare operator bucket naming, now issues a live redirect to www.csquare.com, the operator current domain, confirmed directly this session. Csquare own site states it owns and operates data centers built over decades by developing, acquiring, integrating, and operating advanced data centers, without giving a specific founding or rebrand date on the pages fetched this session. Csquare own site, fetched this session, lists corporate headquarters at 3100 Olympus Blvd, Suite 510, Coppell, TX 75019, and states a current portfolio of 80 total data centers, about 3.5 million square feet, more than 500 MW of power capacity, and more than 36,000 cross connects, across 15 North American markets plus London. On at least two Csquare pages fetched this session, a customer facing portal link pointed to evoquedcs.my.site.com, suggesting some relationship to Evoque Data Center Solutions, though this session found no page stating the exact nature of that relationship, such as whether Centersquare or Csquare is a direct rebrand of Evoque or a separate successor. Separately, this registry also carries an unrelated Cyxtera operator bucket, not part of this batch, already documented by an earlier pass in this registry as tracing to the same May 2017 CenturyLink data center divestiture discussed in this session own Lumen Technologies research, and as acquired by Cologix in 2023 per Cologix own site. This session found no evidence connecting that Cyxtera and Cologix history to the Centersquare, Csquare, or Evoque names researched for this batch, so the two threads are treated as distinct and unconfirmed to be related. This registry also carries a separate Csquare operator bucket, not part of this batch, whose name is now confirmed by the redirect evidence above to very likely be the same current brand as the Centersquare bucket this batch covers, though this session did not merge or rename either bucket, flagging this as an open duplicate operator naming question for a future dedicated pass rather than resolving it unilaterally. This row is one of two registry rows under this operator in Sterling, VA carrying an IAD2 prefixed code, IAD2-A and IAD2-B, whose coordinates in this registry fall within roughly 90 meters of each other. The operator own current market page for Northern Virginia, fetched this session, describes only a single combined Sterling IAD2 facility figure, 35.8 MW of utility power and 48,169 square feet of raised floor, with no A or B subdivision mentioned and no street address published. This session could not determine whether the two clustered registry rows represent two distinct buildings on one campus sharing that single published figure, or an over fragmented recording of what is now marketed as one consolidated facility, so the combined figure is recorded here as market level context only and is not applied as this specific row own individual capacity or square footage, flagged for a future researcher to disaggregate or consolidate as appropriate.

reading.body:
This facility's individual capacity is not published. The operator's market page describes a combined Sterling IAD2 campus at 35.8 MW of utility power and 48,169 square feet of raised floor, but does not subdivide this figure between two registry rows coded IAD2-A and IAD2-B that sit roughly 90 meters apart, leaving it unclear whether this reading describes one building, half a campus, or a fragmented record of a single consolidated facility. Assuming the combined figure applies here and IT load runs at 80 percent of utility power as typical for modern colocation, this site would hold roughly 900 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density. The operator's current portfolio spans 80 data centers across 15 North American markets plus London with more than 500 MW of total power capacity.

Virginia ranks among the largest data center states in the US and publishes 1,375 MW of capacity across 23 facilities. This facility does not appear individually in that published set, placing it outside the state's top 23 by operator disclosure, though it is one of 326 mapped buildings in Virginia. Its status as unpublished capacity in a major hub state makes it difficult to assess directly against peers.

The facility is located in Sterling, Virginia, in the IAD region near Washington DC, a major colocation market. Centersquare, now operating under the Csquare brand, owns or operates this campus as part of a multi-decade portfolio. Whether this building serves hyperscaler AI training, colocation customers, or traditional enterprise workloads is not disclosed in published specifications.
